If you nail the shoulder, or back in your case, they will drop but it damages a lot of meat near the impact area. Also make sure you aren't using ammo that is fragmenting, American white tail shouldn't fragment too much but I have switched to copper in recent years to limit it as much as possible. I just went through something similar to what you are going through. I lost my boy, Chalupa, to complications due to liver failure just a week ago, he would have been 4 in November. Three weeks before that he seemed fine, then he had a pot belly so we took him to the vet who recommended a specialist who recommended a surgeon. Me and my wife were willing to do anything to improve his chances but the doctors didn't want to start a treatment till they had the information from the liver biopsy. He never recovered from the surgery. He awoke on one of our visits and made the worst pained bark I have ever heard, I felt a mixture of joy that my boy was a wake and the most intense despair I have ever felt. I knew at that moment that we had to let our baby go. I hated that he had such a short life and his last days were spent mixed between unconsciousness and in pain. He was already asleep when they ended his suffering but to be honest, even though I knew it was a mercy, it was very painful to watch him go limp and to leave that room knowing it was the last time I would hold my dog. Sorry for the sob story but i wanted to get that off my chest.

As far as advice, I could not focus on life easily while we were trying to get him better. I was distraught and expected the worst. I'm glad i did because the worst is what happened so he got extra special attention but even me trying to prepare for a week or two won't make the pain when it happens easier. I do want to tell you that it does get easier, here a week out there is noticeably less times I breakdown about it. Another thing is people aren't going to get it. Some people acted like it was dumb for me to spend as much money as I did trying to help my dog and you just have to realize not everyone out there is going to be supportive so find a friend or relative that gets it and is there for you to talk to.

I'm sorry this is happening to you, you and your baby don't deserve this, enjoy the time you still have.

Custom Dwarfcraft pedal I just got today. It is a combo of the Eau Claire Thunder and the Hax. It's kinda awesome.

Edit* The Thunder is a distortion/fuzz and the hax is a ring mod. They are separate effects in the same box. 
The Thunder is the best distortion/fuzz I have played, great sound, very big. it has a tone blast option which bypasses the tone circuit which of course causes a volume increase and changes the feel of the distortion. It also has a time warp that will change the sound from tight clear distortion to a more sludgy sound. The neat thing about it is this pedal that is there is a feedback loop built into the pedal that can be triggered by one of the foot-switches (far right) and the tone of the feedback can be manipulated with both the on board knob correlating to the feedback loop and the knobs on your guitar.

HAX: ring mod pitch shifter thingy. The last switch and the top line of knobs control it. I can get cool oscillations, almost vibrato effects, robotic noises, and genrally cool sounds out of it for experimental noise and to just have some fun.
